1#main: The prohibition of working a firstborn and the prohibition of its shearing. In it are 5 seifim. The firstborn is forbidden in shearing and work; and even if he transgressed and sheared it, or plucked by hand, or even if the wool fell off by itself—it is forbidden in benefit forever. Whether it died by itself, or whether they slaughtered it afterward—even by an expert—slaughter does not permit wool that was plucked while alive; but attached wool, slaughter permits it like its flesh.
2#main: If it was plucked while alive and is still entangled in the rest of the wool—that which appears like the rest of the wool is permitted by slaughter; and that which does not appear like the rest of the wool—and its root is turned toward its head—slaughter does not permit it.
3#main: When he comes to slaughter it, or to see its blemish—it is permitted to pluck the wool of the place of slaughter in order to make a place for slaughter (and the wool he plucked is forbidden in benefit) (Beit Yosef in the name of the Rambam). And specifically by hand, but not with a utensil, so that it not appear like shearing.
4#main: The shearing of a firstborn—even the shearing of a blemished firstborn that became mixed with shearing of non-sacred animals, even one in several thousands—all are forbidden, for it is an important matter and is sanctified in any amount.
5#main: A weaver who filled the woof with wool of a firstborn in a garment—the garment is burned. {Rama: Or buried (Tur). And some say specifically if he wove an important thing such as a design in the garment; but if it is not important, it is nullified in the majority (likewise in Tur and Rosh).}
